key_insight: Water adsorption and especially H2O dissociation on g-C3N4 nanosheets can substantially improve optical absorbance and electrical conductance, making the material more promising for photocatalytic water splitting.
engineering_relevance: These results inform the design and screening of g-C3N4-based photocatalysts for cleaner hydrogen production and sustainable energy systems.
method: DFT calculations to benchmark the pristine nanosheet and adsorption states
SCC-DFTB simulations to probe OH and H2O effects on electronic and optical properties
ReaxFF molecular dynamics to model multi-H2O emission and H2 evolution trends
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a computational comparison showing that dissociated water states outperform the pristine nanosheet in both absorbance and conductance.
watch_item: Because the study is simulation-based, real-world performance may differ due to defects, solvent effects, surface contamination, and synthesis-dependent structure.
paper_title: Computational Study of Water Adsorption and Dissociative Mechanisms Impacting g-C3N4's Optical and Electronic Properties
